newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Mobil Australia says freezes fuel capital spending.
newsitem.headline: Mobil Australia says freezes fuel capital spending.

text.p: Mobil Oil Australia Ltd said on Monday it has frozen new capital expenditure commitments in its fuels business because of uncertainty over industry policy.
Mobil Oil Australia, a unit of Mobil Corp, said the government's approach to the industry required greater clarity and consistency.
"We are receiving mixed messages from both the government and the regulators on the future policy for the industry," Mobil Oil Australia chairman P.C. Tan said in a statement.
"Because of this uncertainty we have frozen new capital expenditure commitments in our fuels business."
The anti-monopoly Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) last August handed a proposal for deregulating the industry to the government, which is still considering the report.
The ACCC last week met the four oil majors in Australia to discuss issues surrounding deregulation, which it said should follow the development of more vigorous competition.
An ACCC spokeswoman said the two groups were still working through the implementation of the proposed changes.

The ACCC is concerned about the strength of the relationships between the four oil majors, Mobil, Shell Australia Ltd, BP Australia Ltd, and Ampol, a joint venture between Caltex Australia Ltd and Pioneer International Ltd.
However, Mobil said on Monday that the average return on equity in the industry, at 6.1 percent over the past five years, was below that for other consumer industries.
A Mobil spokesman said the freeze meant planned capital expenditure for 1997 would amount to about A$100 million, compared with A$200 million in 1996.
The A$100 million related to pre-existing commitments, mainly for completion of work at the Altona refinery in Victoria.
"Further investment in the retail chain has been frozen," the spokesman said.
Mobil owns 700 petrol sites in Australia and supplies a further 1,800 throught its refinery at Altona.
BP Australia said earlier this month that competition and flagging profitability at its 800 service stations had forced it to consider the future of its Australian retail operations.
